nodes.name: Water bath reaction
nodes.procedure: A self-supported NiMoO4·xH2O precursor was first grown on copper foam (CF) through a water bath reaction at 90 °C for 8 h using urea and Ni/Mo metal cation sources (see experimental details in the Supporting Information). Urea plays an important role in the synthesis process since OH⁻ from the urea can combine with metal cations to form metal hydroxides in the initial nucleation step and help to form nanorods during the water bath reaction. At least 6 h was required to obtain a homogenous nanorod structure; 8 h was used to ensure complete and uniform growth.

nodes.name: Ammonia reduction
nodes.procedure: The NiMoO4·xH2O precursor was subsequently converted to Ni-MoN through a second ammonia reduction step at 400 °C for 2 h in mixed ammonia-argon gas (see experimental details in the Supporting Information).

nodes.source_text: and it was subsequently converted to Ni-MoN through a second ammonia reduction step at 400 °C for 2 h

The HER catalytic performance of the as-prepared catalysts was evaluated in a typical three-electrode configuration at a scan rate of 1 mV s⁻¹. For HER activity in alkaline water (1 M KOH), the linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) curves in Figure 3a show that our Ni-MoN requires very low overpotentials (η) of 24 and 61 mV to attain current densities of 10 and 100 mA cm⁻²... To achieve large current densities of 500 and 1000 mA cm⁻²... the Ni-MoN catalyst only requires low overpotentials of 104 and 136 mV, respectively. Ni-MoN has a small Tafel slope value of 35.5 mV dec⁻¹

nodes.description: HER performance in 1 M KOH seawater
nodes.source_text: As shown in Figure 3e, ... our Ni-MoN catalyst still exhibits very good HER activity with limited degradation in 1 m KOH seawater electrolyte. Specifically, it requires overpotentials of 29, 66, 128, and 176 mV to attain current densities of 10, 100, 500, and 1000 mA cm⁻², respectively, in 1 m KOH seawater. The corresponding Tafel slope of Ni-MoN in 1 m KOH seawater is 36.8 mV dec⁻¹

nodes.description: HER stability at 100 mA/cm² in 1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: Figure 3g shows the results of long-term stability tests of the Ni-MoN catalyst performed at constant current densities. It can be seen that the potential fluctuation at a current density of 100 mA cm⁻² over 200 h continuous testing in 1 m KOH is only 16 mV

nodes.description: HER stability at 500 mA/cm² in 1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: Furthermore, the Ni-MoN catalyst can work well at the industry-standard current density of 500 mA cm⁻² for over 200 h

nodes.description: HER stability at 500 mA/cm² in 1 M KOH seawater
nodes.source_text: Even in 1 m KOH seawater electrolyte (Figure S28b, Supporting Information), this catalyst can work stably over 100 h at a large current density of 500 mA cm⁻² with an affordable overpotential fluctuation of 47 mV.

nodes.description: HER CV stability in 1 M KOH (19k cycles)
nodes.source_text: after 19 000 (19k) CV cycles in 1 M KOH electrolyte, the resultant LSV curve (orange) shows a slight decline compared with the initial curve (red).

nodes.description: HER CV stability in 1 M KOH seawater (48k cycles)
nodes.source_text: Even after 48k CV cycles in 1 m KOH seawater electrolyte (violet), the required overpotential of the Ni-MoN catalyst only increased by 1, 5, 10, and 13 mV to attain current densities of 10, 100, 500, and 1000 mA cm⁻², respectively

nodes.description: HER in 1 M KOH + 0.5 M NaCl (simulated seawater)
nodes.source_text: the catalytic activity of Ni-MoN in 1 M KOH + 0.5 M NaCl (alkaline simulated seawater) is close to that in 1 m KOH electrolyte.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows hierarchical nanorod–nanoparticle structure with high surface roughness and nanoparticles on nanorod surfaces.
nodes.evidence_snippet: newly formed nanoparticles can be found on the surfaces of these nanorods (Figure 1b,c and Figure S5a–d, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows nanoparticles embedded in nanorod matrix, several to tens of nm diameter.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Detailed TEM and aberration-corrected TEM (ACTEM) images in Figure 1d,e and Figure S6a,b... nanoparticles were embedded in the nanorod matrix and are several to tens of nanometers in diameter.

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED pattern shows (200) and (220) facets of metallic Ni and (202) and (220) facets of MoN.
nodes.evidence_snippet: characteristic (200) and (220) facets of metallic Ni and (202) and (220) facets of MoN can be distinguished within the SAED pattern.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows lattice spacings of 0.176 nm (Ni 200), 0.203 nm (Ni 111), and 0.186 nm (MoN 202); amorphous nanorod matrix with crystalline nanoparticles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: interplanar spacings of the lattice fringes... 0.176... and 0.203 nm... corresponding to the (200) and (111) planes... of metallic Ni... 0.186 nm, which is assigned to the (202) plane of MoN.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS confirms Ni gathers in nanoparticle centers, Mo and N throughout nanorod; amorphous MoN nanorods with metallic Ni nanoparticles containing slight MoN.
nodes.evidence_snippet: elemental Ni gathers in the centers of the nanoparticles, while elemental Mo and N can both be found throughout the entire nanorod.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-EDS mapping confirms elemental distribution of Ni, Mo, N, O in Ni-MoN nanorod.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HAADF EDS mapping images... show that elemental Ni gathers in the centers of the nanoparticles, while elemental Mo and N can both be found throughout the entire nanorod.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD confirms metallic Ni (JCPDS#04-0850) and MoN (JCPDS#25-1367) phases.
nodes.evidence_snippet: main peaks in the XRD pattern of Ni-MoN correspond to metallic nickel (Ni, JCPDS#04-0850) and molybdenum nitride (MoN, JCPDS#25-1367).

nodes.characterization_summary: EPR shows stronger magnetic signal at ≈3515 G (g=2.005) indicating higher concentration of unpaired electrons from defects.
nodes.evidence_snippet: EPR spectrum of Ni-MoN shows a stronger magnetic signal at ≈3515 G (g factor = 2.005) than that of the NiMoO₄·xH₂O precursor.

nodes.characterization_summary: BET surface area of 27.5 m² g⁻¹, three times larger than precursor; type IV hysteresis indicates mesoporous structure with average pore size ≈6.5 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The surface area of Ni-MoN was measured using the Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) method and was found to be 27.5 m² g⁻¹ (Figure 2c), which is three times larger than that of the NiMoO₄·xH₂O precursor (7.6 m² g⁻¹)... nitrogen adsorption–desorption isotherm of Ni-MoN shows a typical IV hysteresis loop, suggesting that it has a mesoporous structure with an average pore size of ≈6.5 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows Ni⁰ at 853.4/870.6 eV, Ni²⁺ at 856.0/873.9 eV, Mo³⁺ at 230.0/233.1 eV, Mo⁴⁺ at 231.3/234.2 eV, Mo⁶⁺ at 232.6/235.7 eV, N-Mo/N-Ni at 397.5 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: two Ni⁰ peaks corresponding to metallic Ni can be observed at 853.4 and 870.6 eV... three doublets were observed: 230.0 and 233.1 (Mo³⁺)... N–Mo or N–Ni at 397.5 eV.
